page: Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing AMD EPYC 7452 processors running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a constrained vCPU design, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at 3.35 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory allocation is dense at 128.0 GB of RAM, equating to 32.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 275 GB of local SSD capacity, while no dedicated graphics accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are present.

Benchmark assessments reflect the constrained compute profile paired with a large memory footprint. In synthetic evaluation, the AMD EPYC architecture delivers an average Geekbench single-core score of 1362.0 and PassMark encryption performance of 4308.61. Multi-threaded compute capacity is limited by the 4-vCPU allocation, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 3187.0 and stress-ng multi-core testing placing in the bottom tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 45.48 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 25.73 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET operations reached 3.63 million operations per second, and static web serving recorded 3.92 GB/sec throughput.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the asymmetric ratio of 32 GB of memory per core offers distinct cost efficiency for database and software workloads governed by per-core licensing. Instead of paying software fees across 16 vCPUs to access 128 GB of RAM, the instance exposes only 4 compute cores. This profile is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise databases, large Redis or Memcached instances, and intermediate data processing pipelines requiring substantial memory residency without intensive parallel CPU requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4as_v4 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for workloads requiring high memory capacity with minimal core counts. Powered by AMD EPYC 7452 processors on the x86_64 architecture at 3.35 GHz, the virtual machine provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 32.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates 275 GB of local SSD storage and operates without dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark results show moderate single-core efficiency, with a Geekbench single-core rating of 1362.0, while multi-core processing is constrained by the 4-thread environment. Memory throughput sustains 45.48 GB/sec for uncached reads. This configuration creates significant qualitative cost advantages for software stacks with per-core licensing restrictions that require large memory footprints, making it suitable for memory-heavy databases, caching layers, and in-memory analytics.
